articleTitle: Evaluation of CO2 Emissions by Water Pumping Scheduling with Water Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In recent years, the amount of the photovoltaic (PV) system has been rapidly increasing from the viewpoint of carbon neutral. There are growing needs for efforts to reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission by effectively utilizing surplus electricity from PVs and promoting local production for local consumption. In order to address these issues, this study focused on the electric demand control of water supply pumps in the water distribution system, which is infrastructure equipment for consumers. By controlling the start/stop of the water pump considering PV generation condition, it is expected to contribute to the reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission from the electricity used by the pump. Therefore, this paper proposes an optimal operation planning method for water pumps to reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission using a mixed integer linear programming problem. The control targets are the start/stop of the water pumps and amount of water demand response (DR) in each time-slot. The water DR also improves the flexibility of the water distribution system. The effectiveness of proposed method and water DR is evaluated in terms of reduction of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission and the operation of water pump. As a result, water DR improved flexibility of water distribution system and reduced CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission because operating more pumps on sunny days and fewer pumps on rainy days.

articleTitle: Necessity and Strategy Analysis of Installing Arrester for Overvoltage Suppression of GIL
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Gas insulated metal enclosed transmission lines (GIL) are widely used in the field of long distance and large capacity transmission, but there is a lack of lightning protection design research for long distance GIL. In this paper, we build an overhead wire-GIL hybrid transmission line simulation model, and study the influence of different transient voltages on long distance GIL lightning overvoltage. The results show that when the amplitude of lightning current is 20 kA and the total length of GIL is 15 km, the minimum peak lightning overvoltage generated on GIL line is over 1930 kV, which is greater than the lightning impulse limit voltage of 500 kV GIL. Therefore, lightning arresters need to be installed to ensure the safe and reliable operation of GIL transmission line. Furthermore, the suppression effect of different installation positions of the arrester on the lightning overvoltage of the long-distance GIL is studied. The protective effect of installing the arrester at the first and last ends respectively, installing the arrester in the middle and installing the arrester at the first and last ends respectively is analyzed. The results show that when only one arrester is installed, the minimum GIL overvoltage occurs at the location where the arrester is installed. The end overvoltage peak value of the arrester installed in the middle position is greater than that of the end overvoltage peak value of the arrester installed in the first and last two ends respectively, and the overvoltage protection effect is poor. The protective effect of installing a lightning arrester at both ends of the GIL is obviously better than that of installing only one end of the GIL. The research results provide a theoretical basis for the design of lightning protection measures for long distance GIL.

articleTitle: Improved Low Voltage Ride-Through Capability of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator Wind Turbine based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The integration of large-scale intermittent renewable energy sources imposes many difficulties in maintaining grid stability and reliability. When considering wind turbine-based power facilities, the ability of these systems to stay connected to the grid throughout a fault or prolonged voltage drop is known as Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT). This paper suggests an approach to improve this capability, focusing on Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators (PMSG) wind turbines based on the Model Predictive Control (MPC) controller. The Model Predictive Control unit will enhance the turbine’s response using a predictive algorithm, which feeds the predicted signals into a cost function that brings them into compliance with the desired reference value. By using an iterative loop to investigate the switching states of the Grid-Side Converter (GSC), the proposed controller assists the grid-side converter in providing the best switching signal to accelerate voltage recovery on the DC-link voltage, provide additional reactive power as well as ensure good output power quality to support the grid. The results of the method have been verified through Simulink/Matlab simulation software. The benefits of the proposed approach are better wind turbine responsiveness during the start and end of the fault, and successful LVRT management utilizing the modified grid-side converter.

articleTitle: Combining Fuzzy Logic and Discrete Wavelet Transform for Accurate Fault and Inrush Current Classification in High Voltage Capacitor Banks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The high voltage capacitor bank is a critical component in substations, essential for maintaining power quality and system stability. However, these banks are susceptible to faults and inrush currents, posing significant operational challenges. This paper presents a method for accurately classifying fault and inrush currents in high voltage capacitor banks using Fuzzy Logic and Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). The DWT decomposes current waveforms into frequency components, enabling the extraction of features that characterize faults and inrush currents. These features are processed by a Fuzzy Inference System (FIS), which classifies the events based on predefined rules and membership functions. The integration of DWT and FIS provides a robust framework for distinguishing between different types of faults and inrush currents with high accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed method’s efficacy, showing improved performance in classification accuracy and noise robustness compared to traditional techniques. This research enhances monitoring and protection systems in power networks, ensuring more reliable operation of high voltage capacitor banks. Implementing this method allows for better fault management and minimized downtime, leading to improved overall system efficiency and stability.

articleTitle: Adaptive Thermal Management Strategy of Fuel Cell Vehicle Systems with Environmental Adaptability
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Thermal management of proton exchange membrane fuel cells plays a crucial role in the long-term stable operation of fuel cell vehicle systems. Existing thermal management strategies ignore the key role of system component characteristic constraints in reducing the influence of thermal perturbations from the vehicle’s exterior environment, making it challenging to achieve the desired control results. In this study, an active adaptive coupled thermal management strategy is proposed. It considers the changing thermal environment and the component characteristics of the thermal management system. The approach combines particle filter estimation, closed-loop model predictive control, and fuzzy control to regulate the critical components of the thermal management system and act in concert to optimize the thermal management of the fuel cell. Compared with the closed-loop model predictive control alone, the strategy proposed in this study reduces the average errors of the stack’s coolant inlet and outlet temperatures by $\mathbf{3 9 . 9 \%}$ and $30.5 \%$, respectively. The proposed active thermal management strategy exhibits excellent performance in an external thermal environment with unpredictable disturbances.

articleTitle: Synthetic Load Modelling Considering the Influence of Distributed Small Hydropower Units
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Load modeling plays an important role in power system security and stability analysis and accurate simulation calculation. Grid-connected small hydropower stations are important active and reactive power sources in the distribution network. The influence of a large number of small hydropower stations on the load model has not been considered in the previous load model, and the original traditional load model can no longer accurately characterize the dynamic characteristics of the load area with small hydropower stations. In this paper, the working mechanism and interaction mechanism of small hydropower units on the load side are studied, and a generalized load integration equivalent modeling method considering small hydropower units is proposed. In this method, a small hydropower generator model is added to the comprehensive load model considering the distribution network, and a dynamic equivalence method considering the small hydropower units is proposed, which realizes the accurate simulation of the characteristics outside the power supply area of the load with small hydropower units, and provides strong technical support for the accurate simulation, analysis and decision-making of the new power system.

articleTitle: Charging Demand Forecast of Electric Vehicles Considering Charging Management Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With the continuous increase in electric vehicles (EVs) penetration, charging facilities are becoming critical growth points for urban grid development. However, the simultaneous charging of numerous EVs results in dramatic load fluctuations, posing a substantial challenge to the distribution network’s capacity to accommodate charging loads. To address these challenges and the current research gap, an EV charging load prediction model is proposed in this paper, which considers a peak charging management strategy. Firstly, the Monte Carlo method is used to obtain the spatial-temporal distribution of EV users, integrating their behavioral characteristics and energy consumption model. Then, the charging pile selection model of EV users is established by comprehensively considering their parking duration, starting charge state, and next driving mileage. On this basis, a peak charging management strategy is proposed to predict the charging demand of EV users, which improves the distribution network’s acceptance of charging loads during peak hours. Finally, an area in a southern city is selected for case analysis to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integration of Photovoltaic and Battery Storage System by Using Voltage Source Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Solar energy has penetrated small as well as large power systems and has been growing steadily. In this paper, a small system containing PV generation, battery, and an inverter is considered. It can be operated in grid-connected or standalone modes. Moreover, this system can be controlled by a combination of a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller, bidirectional converter, and Voltage Source Controller (VSC). The PV output is determined by solar irradiation and ambient temperature. It is important to extract PV generation at its maximum power. Several MPPT controllers can be employed to achieve maximum power. In this paper, we have chosen to use Perturb and Observe (P&O) controller. Also, a bidirectional converter is required to regulate the DC-side power flow. VSC can interface with a three-phase network when synchronized with the network. It can also maintain Unity Power Factor (UPF) in grid-connected mode. An Inductor-Capacitor-Inductor (LCL) filter can reduce the harmonics in voltages and currents after conversion. MATLAB/Simulink toolbox R-2020a is utilized to simulate the entire system.

articleTitle: Design of Wide-Area Multi-Mode Controller Using Genetic Algorithm for Power System Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In wide-area power systems managing frequency and stability is crucial particularly given the complexities of interconnected networks and vast distances. The introduction of advanced control strategies is essential to enhance resilience, reliability, and stability across the network. This paper present an approach that integrates a wide area multi mode controller which is optimized using a genetic algorithm. The wide area Multi-mode controller(MMC) is implemented in the IEEE 9-bus system as a standard studying system. This study meticulously evaluates the MMC’s performance and resilience in damping frequency oscillations under several challenging and critical scenarios including short circuits, communication latency, and failures in protection devices during these events and compared to others supplementary controllers. The results demonstrate that the MMC has best performance effectively in damping the oscillation mode within the system under critical conditions among the other controllers even when facing latency in communication and protection control signals.

articleTitle: Study of Current Distribution Characteristics of Automotive Fuel Cells with High-resolution Segmented Measurement Device
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) has the advantages of low operating temperature, fast start-up, high power density, etc., which has a wide application prospect in the field of automotive power. The fuel cell performance can be analyzed under different current densities by using the zonal current collection detection technique. However, the existing method has low resolution and cannot accurately reflect the current distribution inside the automotive fuel cell stack. In this paper, a high-resolution segmented measurement device with 396 points is used to experimentally test the local current density distribution characteristics of a 406 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> automotive fuel cell during a stepwise increase in load current, and the results are presented in three-dimensional data. The experimental results show that when the load current is 0.1 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the current density at the hydrogen inlet is significantly higher than that at the oxygen inlet, with the highest current density of 0.154 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the lowest of 0.0489 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>; when the load current is 0.6A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the current density at the oxygen inlet is higher than that at the hydrogen inlet, with the highest current density of 0.926 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the lowest current density of 0.375 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a difference of 0.551 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The precise analysis of the current density distribution characteristics using the high-resolution segmented current collection measurement technique is of great importance in studying the control strategy of the fuel cell system and diagnosing the failure.

articleTitle: Active Distribution Network Differential Protection Scheme Based on Harmonic Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of inverter-interfaced distributed generation (IIDG), the short-circuit current characteristics of distribution networks have changed, making traditional protection methods difficult to meet the safety operation requirements of distribution networks. Therefore, a differential protection scheme based on harmonic current injection is proposed. Firstly, IIDG is used as the source of harmonic signal injection, and the characteristics of its faults and the principles for selecting parameters of harmonic signals are introduced. Then, the distribution network is divided into zones, suitable harmonic injections from distributed energy sources are selected, and the amplitude characteristics of harmonics are analyzed to differentiate between internal and external faults of the lines. After the analysis, protection criteria are established based on the differences in harmonic current amplitudes during internal and external faults. Finally, the action performance of the proposed method is simulated and verified in PSCAD/EMTDC, demonstrating that the scheme can still respond quickly and effectively during different faults.

articleTitle: Modelling of Green Energy System in Pulau Perhentian
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The use of renewable energy systems for island power production is the most environmentally friendly option. The motivation to use renewable energy resources has grown in recent decades due to concerns about global warming and the depletion of fossil fuels. Diesel prices are also rising and are expected to continue to do so in the future. This is a challenge for rural areas, especially off-grid islands, which are far from the grid and have high costs associated with extending the grid to reach them. This study proposes a solution to generate clean and environmentally friendly power on the isolated island of Pulau Perhentian Kecil, Terengganu, using renewable energy. The green energy system will be comprised of intermittent renewable energy sources, solar and wind energy. The system is designed to be costeffective and efficient. Solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbines have a high potential for use on the island because they are abundant and accessible. They also have the potential to reduce carbon emissions in the long term. The Hybrid Optimisation Model for Electrical Renewables (HOMER) software was used to simulate and analyze the hybrid system. The study results showed that the PV and wind turbine system had a net present cost (NPC) savings of around RM 37.8 million. The renewable energy portion was also determined to be 48 percent, which is a key metric for assessing environmental impact. Additionally, the optimal outcome of this system was a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by a total of 47 percent. The findings of this study suggest that renewable energy systems are a viable option for power production on isolated islands. They are more cost-effective and environmentally friendly than diesel generators, and they have the potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and also provides a roadmap for the development of renewable energy systems on off-grid islands.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Forecasting Dielectric Permittivity in Nanodielectrics for Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Accurate prediction of dielectric permittivity is crucial for developing nanodielectric materials with advanced properties, which are largely used in pulse power systems due to their promising power density. To further explore its potential, four ML algorithms, including linear regression, support vector machines (SVM), Gaussian process regression (GPR), and boosted trees were utilized for predicting the dielectric permittivity of the nanodielectric materials. To train the model, milling time, particle size, as well as filler volume faction, are considered as the training parameters (also known as features). Then, the effective dielectric permittivity of the nanodielectric is predicted as the output of the ML models. The results showed that the rational Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) algorithm offered the best performance. These approaches have the potential to provide more accurate dielectric permittivity predictions than conventional methods, as they take a variety of parameters into account. Furthermore, the proposed models can be readily adapted to different materials, making them versatile and useful tools in the prediction of dielectric permittivity.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations with Two Types of Charging Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With the accelerated popularity of electric vehicles (EVs) and the large-scale construction of charging networks, charging facilities with different rates can satisfy diverse charging demands. A planning model of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) with two types of charging facilities is proposed. Firstly, two scenarios of spatial-temporal distribution of charging demands are simulated based on dynamic traffic network and users’ routing and charging behavior. Secondly, with distribution network operation constraints considered, planning model to minimize annual total cost of the whole charging system is formulated and then converted to a mixed integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) problem. Finally, case studies on the 26-node transportation system and IEEE 33-bus distribution system have confirmed the effectiveness to solve the planning problem of electric vehicle charging stations with two types of charging facilities.

articleTitle: Smoothing of Intermittent Solar Photovoltaic Output Power by Controlling Battery Converter with Simple Moving Average Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Solar energy is increasingly recognized as an important future energy source due to its abundant availability and renewable nature. However, the intermittent nature of solar energy can cause fluctuations in the produced electricity, making it difficult to guarantee a stable and reliable electricity supply. One solution that can be implemented is to use batteries in a photovoltaic solar power plant system with a Simple Moving Average (SMA) control algorithm, which can help in smoothing and reducing fluctuations in the solar power. The parameter that can be adjusted in the SMA algorithm is the Window Size (WS) or the arithmetic averaging width of the photovoltaic output power over time. This research evaluates the effect of changing WS value in the SMA algorithm on the resulting smoothed photovoltaic output power, and the technical effects on batteries. Based on the results of evaluation, the increase of WS value will slow down the response of photovoltaic output power to changes in irradiation and increase the smoothing quality of the intermittent photovoltaic output power. In addition, increasing the WS will reduce the maximum power received on the load side, and the amount of energy used by the battery during the power smoothing process will increase, resulting in the increase of required battery capacity.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing and Placement of BESS in Distribution Grid with High PV Penetration Considering BESS Optimal Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs) are an effective solution in preventing overvoltage caused by the high penetration rate of renewable energy sources (RES). This paper proposes a new strategy to achieve voltage regulation in distributed power systems in the presence of solar sources and BESSs. The goal is to find the minimum size of the BESSs and their corresponding position in the network based on the size and location of the integrated solar generation. The proposed method formulates the problem by combining grid sensitivity coefficient analysis and modeling second-order cone programming (SOCP) in power flow analysis. Using reactive power to adjust voltage regulation is not always the optimal solution in distribution systems in which $R / X$ is large. Therefore, the study only considers the minimum size and best BESS location achieved by optimizing the amount of solar-curtailed active power through BESS based on the grid topology and $R / X$ ratios in the distribution system. Simulation results on the modified IEEE-33 bus verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Implementation of SCADA in a distribution system with a medium voltage motor as load
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With the growth of the industry and the need for higher capacity motors, the need arises to implement monitoring, control and protection systems called SCADA in distribution networks. A protection adjustment methodology is proposed and its implementation in a SCADA with IEC61850 communication between five IEDs. GOOSE, MMS and SV messaging was implemented between the IEDs of the network. The system includes a subtransmission network, a distribution network and a dynamic load of a medium voltage motor. The methodology is validated by injecting fault and steady-state voltages and currents using the OMICRON CMC356 equipment. Communication times, response times of protection functions and tripping of the circuit breaker are verified.

articleTitle: Investigation of data center cooling operation using ground thermal utilization thermal storage tank
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This research examines a system that utilizes shallow ground thermal utilization and thermal storage tank for data center cooling, focusing on improving energy efficiency and sustainability in response to increasing digital demands. This study evaluates the effectiveness and potential cost savings of the system, advocating for its adoption as an innovative solution for environmentally friendly and economical data center operations. Simulation results indicate that the condition in which a underground thermal storage tank was installed and the cold heat was stored and released in accordance with fluctuations in electricity rates resulted in a reduction in electricity rates of more than 1 million yen (more than $1.5 \%$) compared to the condition without a underground thermal storage tank.

articleTitle: Virtual Energy Storage System Using Energy Management with Flexible Load for Capacity Reserve
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Peak demand is expected to increase due to population growth, climate change, evolving lifestyles, and technology advancements, leading to the necessity of investing more network equipment to handle these peak periods. While Energy Storage Systems (ESS) could address this, their high capital investment poses a challenge. Thus, a Virtual Energy Storage System (VESS) emerges as a cost-effective solution. A VESS uses flexible loads like air conditioners to manage energy demand in real-time. Instead of physical storage, VESS adjusts appliance energy consumption based on grid conditions. This paper presents the development of a VESS prototype using a flexible load to provide similar functions to ESS. By coordinating the demand response from the air conditioner, it aims to store and release energy, thereby increasing the flexibility of the end user’s load and increasing the capacity reserve of the building. The results show that the proposed VESS, coordinating the demand response from the air conditioner, can achieve an energy reduction of $21.74 \%$. The system adjusts air conditioner settings based on outdoor temperatures, consuming more energy in cooler mornings and less in warmer afternoons, mimicking the behavior of an energy storage system (ESS), thereby increasing the flexibility of the end user’s load and the capacity reserve of the building.

articleTitle: Optimizing Photovoltaic Power Distribution for EV Charging in EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) powered Electric Vehicles Charging Station (EVCS) are currently being extensively deployed in power system networks. Nevertheless, effectively distributing PV power for the charging of many Electric Vehicles (EVs) remains difficult due to the varying State Of Charge (SOC) of each EV upon arrival at the EVCS and the plan to achieve a desired SOC when departing from the EVCS. This study proposes an Energy Management System (EMS) approach for dispersed PV units to charge EVs in a way that ensures the EVs reach their targeted SOC. This research will include the power flow between PV units, the utility grid, and EVs. Moreover, the detailed profit for the owner of EVCS will also be presented.

articleTitle: A Seamless Switching Control Method of DAB Converters for Photovoltaic Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper proposes a seamless switching control method for dual active bridge (DAB) converters applied in islanded photovoltaic microgrids to suppress bus voltage drops and achieve voltage self-recovery. First, the voltage and current on both sides of the converter are selected as the control objectives, and a parallel proportional-integral (PI) controller is presented to obtain multiple quasi control signals. Secondly, a two-stage decision-making scheme is proposed to obtain the optimal control signal based on the multiple loop outputs. To improve the dynamic performance of the system, a synchronous updating method is adopted to improve the conventional PI control structure. Combined with the application scenarios in the photovoltaic microgrids, the impact of the proposed method on the system stability is analyzed. Finally, compared with the conventional switching control method, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Smart House Considering Water Temperature in Hot Water Storage Tank
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Due to the recent global situation, consumers are required to reduce energy consumption, and smart houses equipped with solar power generation, heat pumps, etc. are being proposed. However, in previous our studies, the hot water in the hot water storage tank was treated as one layer to meet the heat demand, which sometimes resulted in excessive use of thermal energy. In this research, we minimize the thermal energy used by modeling the water temperature inside the hot water storage tank.

articleTitle: Simplified Analysis and Validation of a Two-switch Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper presents a simplified analysis and validation of a two-switch flyback converter. When parasitic components, i.e. the MOSFET’s output capacitance and transformer’s leakage inductance, are neglected, circuit analysis of the two-switch flyback converter is greatly simplified and derivation of the converter equations becomes straightforward. The validity of the derived equations, which are useful for the converter design, is confirmed by simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Light-Emitting Diode Luminaire For Two-Lanes Roadway Lighting System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Lighting systems for roadways are an important aspect of the transportation system in terms of safety and providing comfort for drivers. Conventional lighting systems use high-pressure sodium luminaires, which consume a lot of energy. This paper proposes an evaluation of roadway lighting using lightemitting diodes (LEDs) as luminaires. The paper uses a two-lane road as a case study and simulates the lighting parameters using DIALux software. The case study varies the wattage of the luminaires, pole distances, and pole arrangements, while keeping the pole specifications fixed. The parameters under consideration include illuminance, luminance, and uniformity on the road surface. Additionally, the results are compared with international criteria standards to confirm that the selected LED luminaires can provide the necessary lighting quality for road usage. The results show that LED luminaires can provide lighting quality within standard criteria. However, different pole arrangements require different levels of wattage and pole distances. Therefore, the selection of LEDs needs to match the design of pole distances and arrangements to provide sufficient roadway lighting.

articleTitle: Distributed Event-Triggered Secure Control of Islanded AC Microgrids under Cyber-Switched Networks Against Simultaneous DoS Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This article introduces an enhanced secondary control method utilizing a Distributed Event-Triggered Secure Mechanism (DETSM) designed for AC autonomous MGs operating under switching communication topologies and subject to simultaneous Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. The proposed non-synchronous event-based cyber-security strategy aims to improve communication efficiency and reduce the consumption of network resources, with a particular focus on mitigating DoS attacks initiated by multiple adversaries and it is proved that no Zeno behavior occurs. In addition, this study investigates the contribution of both Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in Ac MGs. Finally, the performance of the proposed control scheme is evaluated by a simulation through different scenarios in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: A Method for Synchronous Error Correction of Multiple Influences in Power Energy Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The accuracy of power energy measurement is crucial for the economy and reliability of power systems, directly affecting the economic benefits of the power system and the fairness to users. However, different errors arise under various conditions, such as voltage, current, frequency, power factor, and temperature. This paper investigates the impact of multiple influencing factors on the measurement error of electric energy and proposes a method for synchronous error correction based on multiple influencing factors. By constructing a multidimensional error correction model, this method achieves error correction under arbitrary parameter conditions, thereby improving the accuracy of smart meter detection.

articleTitle: Optimal Management of EV Charging Stations Based on Scale Considerations
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a need to reduce greenhouse gases emissions in order to achieve a decarbonized society. In order to achieve decarbonization, the introduction of electric vehicles (EVs), which do not emit CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, will be effective. Combining the Park & Ride concept to reduce traffic congestion and EV charging station with renewable energy can also reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. In this study, a parking station in Okinawa Prefecture will be used as a model. The model includes renewable energy generation facilities and energy storage systems and simulates the optimization of the annual operation of the parking station, with EVs as the target. The amount of electricity generated by renewable energy is predicted by model predictive control, and the charge and discharge schedule of the energy storage system is determined based on the power generation data. Then, comparing the off-grid operation case and the grid-connected case, and discussing under what conditions the annual profit will be higher. According to the results, off-grid profits are higher in cases with high electricity demand, while on-grid profits are higher in cases with low electricity demand.

articleTitle: Research on Mechanical Fault Diagnosis of High-Voltage Circuit Breaker Based on Attention Parallel Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high-voltage circuit breaker mechanical fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a highvoltage circuit breaker mechanical fault diagnosis model based on attention parallel acceleration by taking advantage of the correlation between the vibration signal and the mechanical state. First of all, the vibration signal feature extraction is realized through the convolutional neural network architecture of onedimensional aggregated attention mechanism; at the same time, the Laplace factor carried by the one-dimensional feature itself is used to construct the Laplace parallel acceleration channel architecture, which accelerates the convergence rate of the model; finally, the distribution of the same category of correlated subdomains is adjusted by combining the domain migration learning and the local adaptation algorithm to get the classification of vibration signals, and the three types of mechanical faults, such as closing spring and fatigue failure, are diagnosed efficiently. The vibration signal classification is obtained to effectively diagnose three types of mechanical failures, such as the fatigue failure of the closing spring. The experimental results show that the average accuracy of this model is more than $2 \%$ higher than that of existing detection methods, and its inference speed is at least $18 \%$ higher than that of existing one-dimensional convolutional neural networks under the condition of not exceeding $\pm 1 \%$ accuracy range interval.

articleTitle: Research on the Aging Characteristics of Optical Fiber Sensors in High-Temperature Insulating Oil
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: As critical power system equipment, the oil-immersed transformer has a particular application prospect in realizing the in-situ monitoring of transformer physical quantities by implanting distributed optical fiber inside the transformer. To ensure the reliability of optical fiber sensing, this paper studies the sensing characteristics of optical fiber in a high-temperature insulating oil environment. Through the real transformer’s accelerated aging test, the optical fiber’s accelerated aging inside the transformer is realized, and several tests are carried out on the optical fiber after the aging test. The calibration results of Brillouin temperature and strain response coefficient show that the response coefficient changes little before and after aging, the fiber loss increases after the aging test, and the Brillouin scattering spectrum of the aged fiber does not change significantly. At the same time, the surface microstructure of the sheath is studied by optical camera and scanning electron microscope, and the sensing fiber’s reliability in the transformer’s aging process is verified.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Transformer-less Solar Powered Quadratic Boost Converter based Grid Tie Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This study presents a design for a pure sinusoidal wave grid-tie inverter (GTI) intended for photovoltaic (PV) applications. The suggested GTI utilizes a quadratic boost converter (dual triggered), a single-stage buck regulator, an H-bridge inverter, and a passive filter circuit. GTI power circuit switching utilizes sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) for grid synchronization situations. The proposed inverter, which does not use any transformer significantly decreases output current Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) meeting standard requirements and reduces the inverter’s size. The passive filter circuit maintains a consistent output current to stabilize the system immediately. The suggested inverter’s overall performance is simulated using PSIM software based on the designed values of circuit components. The simulation results demonstrate that the suggested inverter not only eliminates higher order harmonics but also showcases compact size, and cost-effectiveness as it does not require any isolating equipment’s.

articleTitle: Medium-term Electric Network Planning Using SARIMA: EERSA Case Study - Ecuador
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This article analyzes the future electricity consumption of Empresa Eléctrica Riobamba S.A. (EERSA) in Ecuador, specifically in the residential, industrial, and commercial sectors. Time series models like ARMA, ARIMA, and SARIMA are utilized to make medium-term predictions, and Matlab software is used to design the models and make demand predictions. The data used to make these predictions comes from historical information held by EERSA, spanning from January 2001 to November 2022. The predicted electricity demand closely matches the original demand in the residential and commercial sectors before 2020. Still, there has been a significant variation in recent years due to atypical events like the COVID-19 pandemic. Similarly, the prediction results for the industrial sector align with the original demand before 2018, but the pandemic has affected demand after that date. Notably, this sector has a distinct characteristic due to significant consumers, such as Cemento Chimborazo company, which has caused considerable variation in electricity demand since 2018.

articleTitle: MPC-based Optimal Operation of Smart City Considering Seasonally Adjusted Parameter
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: To achieve a decarbonized society, cities are transitioning to smart cities. Instead of large-scale thermal power generation, with its low thermal efficiency, comprehensive energy management integrating renewable energy source (RES) and combined cooling and heating power generation (CCHP) is being studied. In recent years, model predictive control (MPC), which calculates the optimization including future states and solves the problem based on receding horizon, has attracted attention as a way to deal with the uncertainties of RES. However, since the prediction horizon ($N_{p}$) is fixed in normal MPC operation, seasonal variations are not considered. MPC operation can be further improved by selecting the $N_{p}$ appropriately and varying it adaptively. In this study, we propose an optimal operation based on MPC that applies different forecast intervals for different seasons, and verify its effectiveness by comparing costs and carbon emissions through simulations.

articleTitle: SolarMatic: A Responsive Solar Tracking Solution Using IoT and Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The purpose of solar panel sun tracking is to align the panels with the path of the sun during the day in order to maximize the productivity and efficiency of solar energy systems. Solar panel sun tracking methods fall into two main categories: sensor-based and astronomical. Different types have different benefits and cons depending on the use and surroundings. This theoretical framework creates SolarMatic, a responsive solar tracking system by integrating IoT sensors, actuators, and data analytics. This cutting-edge system not only increases energy output and increases the return on investment for solar systems, but it also reduces reliance on non-renewable energy sources, contributing to a more sustainable and environmentally friendly future. The final goal is to compare and assess the two tracking strategies, then dynamically select the one that produces the highest power production. The technology allows for remote monitoring and control because of its smooth communication with cloud-based servers.

articleTitle: GFM inverter control considering dynamic voltage stability in power systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This study proposes a GFM inverter control method that takes into account the dynamic voltage stability of the power system. Conventional GFM inverters set active and reactive power command values based on frequency and voltage droop characteristics, which may result in inappropriate compensation for load increase. In the proposed method, the critical boundary index (CBI), an index of voltage stability, is used to determine the active and reactive command values of the transmission line so that the operating point approaches the origin from the stability limit plane. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by comparison with the conventional droop method. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves dynamic voltage stability over the conventional method.

articleTitle: An Optimized Gas Supply Strategy for Startup-shutdown Processes in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Frequent start-stop is a key factor affecting fuel cells’ operating lifespan. Optimized startup-shutdown strategies, such as well-designed gas supply and residual hydrogen depletion procedures, can effectively alleviate this impact. This study introduces a gas supply method that optimizes the shutdown process and also considers the post-shutdown residual gas state, which influences the design of the subsequent startup strategy. Specifically, this research suggests initiating shutdown by deactivating the cathode first, followed by the anode after the complete discharge. For startup, it recommends supplying hydrogen into the anode initially, followed by air into the cathode. The gas diffusion model and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy maintains a maximum pressure difference of only 25 kPa between the anode and cathode during the shutdown. Furthermore, it yields a maximum voltage deviation of merely 80 mV during voltage release, with all cell voltages surpassing 0.8 V within 1 second without causing hydrogen-air interface issues. This approach ensures the safety of fuel cell startup and shutdown and extends stack lifetime.

articleTitle: On Equivalent Inertia of a Modern Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper addresses an updated discussion on estimating the equivalent inertia in a modern power grid with high penetration of converter-based distributed generators and renewable energy sources. Unlike conventional power grids, the equivalent inertia of a modern power grid is not constant; thus, it cannot be calculated straightforwardly by simply summation of inertia from the existing bulk synchronous generators. Some data-driven concepts are introduced to calculate the equivalent inertia of the grid, containing not only physical inertia but also virtual inertia provided by the grid-forming converters.

articleTitle: Aggregated Model of Load, Grid Forming, and Grid Following Inverters for an Unbalanced System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The distribution system is known for its inherent unbalanced nature and complex modelling. To decrease complexity when modeling the system to evaluate the dynamic analysis, the aggregated model is developed for load, grid following control inverter-based resource (IBR), and grid forming control IBR. Furthermore, to consider the imbalance of the system, the approximation methodology to estimate the parameters of each phase is proposed for each aggregated model. The proposed approach significantly contributes to the field by offering a simplified yet accurate method for dynamic analysis of unbalanced distribution systems. Validation of the approach is performed through study cases on the IEEE 13-bus system and the known parameters, limited to only the voltage and current of each phase at the connection point and each component’s total power. Furthermore, the dynamic response of the aggregated model is compared to the actual system of IEEE 13 -bus. The results indicate that the unparameterized aggregated model exhibits significant error, while the response of the parameterized aggregated model is similar to that of the actual system, validating the effectiveness of the proposed parameter estimation methodology.

articleTitle: Research on Application and Control Technologies of the Embedded HVDC in a Provincial Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: To achieve the goals of a novel power system of “clean and low-carbon, safe and controllable, flexible and efficient, intelligent and friendly, open and interactive”, the proportion of renewable energy in the system should further increase. As a typical provincial power grid, Jiangsu power system in China intends to realize larger renewable energy integration and consumption, which is also better to adapt power supply shortages and reformed energy consumption assessment. The embedded HVDC is considered to be applied to increase power transmission within the grid for renewable energy development in the provincial power grid. The feasibility to construct the embedded HVDC and the ability to enhance the transmission capacity are analyzed. The control technologies are devised to realize regular large power transmission and improve security of the grid. Simulation results verify the feasibility and proposed control of the embedded HVDC in a provincial power grid.

articleTitle: Further Experiments in Integrating Transparent Photovoltaic Film with Transparent Vacuum Insulation Panel
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This study continued the authors’ previous work on integrating photovoltaic panels to structured core Transparent Vacuum Insulation Panels, with the goal of determining the effect that seasonal differences in humidity would have on the insulation quality of the panels. Measurements were taken with simulated winter and summer conditions by using a climate-controlled chamber for temperature control, and a halogen light set at a distance corresponding to a solar radiation of 1000 watts per square meter. It was determined that the panels manufactured during winter had 30-40 percent lower thermal conductivity, showing the importance of proper climate control during the manufacturing process. A vacuum sealing machine with an in-built heating function during the vacuum cycle is likely required to reach the best quality of panels.

articleTitle: Cost-based Optimal Design and Scheduling Operation of Hybrid Energy Stations in South Korea Using Battery Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The recent rapid increase in electric vehicles (EVs) and EV charging stations has led to the emergence of hybrid energy stations (ESs) that combine photovoltaic systems ($\mathbf{P V}$) and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) to produce power with optimized efficiency. Various types of ESs with different operational methods are being studied. This paper proposes an optimal sizing design and operation method for an ES, from the perspective of BESS operational modes, for cost optimization. The proposed algorithm divides the BESS modes into charging, discharging, and idle states based on the price differentials of peak times, system marginal price (SMP), and EV time of use (TOU), as well as the trend of EV arrivals. Using this algorithm, the optimal sizes of PV and BESS are determined, and the operation of BESS is analyzed. We hope that this paper will be helpful in cost optimization study of hybrid ESs.

articleTitle: Research on Remote Calibration System for Energy Meters
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In this paper, an energy meter remote calibration system based on the principle of “watt-second method” is designed. The voltage, current and pulse data of the measured energy meter are sampled by the on-site terminal and transmitted to the cloud server via 4G network or storage media to get the error of the measured energy meter. This remote calibration method effectively makes up for the shortcomings of the current on-site inspection of power meters and creates a new inspection mode.

articleTitle: Feature-Based Fault Detection and Localization Scheme for Cascaded Multilevel Converter with Multiple Switching Devices Failure in a Submodule
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: A cascaded multilevel converter consists of many submodules (SMs), and thus it has superior advantages such as scalability and redundancy. However, the internal fault probability due to the switching device failure increases with the number of SMs. Several conventional schemes detect the fault and localize the failed SM by using the harmonics whose frequency is equal to the triangular carrier. However, the conventional scheme may not detect the fault when multiple switching devices fail in a SM. This paper proposes the scheme that solves this problem. The features compared with the conventional scheme are as follows: sawtooth carriers are used for phase-shift PWM, and the harmonics with twice the carrier frequency is used for the fault detection and localization. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis for SVC sizing - Study Case: 500kV Ecuadorian Electric Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Static Var Compensators (SVC) connected to a 500 kV radial line used to provide a limited range of instability and balance on a medium size grid operating at 230 kV. The study demonstrates the advantages of linking SVC or other reactive controllers to the network’s elevated operating voltage. Also, by implementing one main strong interconnection between two independent electrical zones, it will be possible to obtain the best possible location for the reactive control system in order to avoid local collapse as well as interarea dragging, resulting in an eventual disconnection. To do so, it will be considered the dynamic stability analysis of the Ecuadorian Electric Grid (SNI) as a baseline to define the stability limits based on different contingencies. Followed by the run of contingencies that showed the most suitable point to implement SVC based on the reactive power flow commonly higher on S/E Chorrillos, as well as scale the reactive requirements of the equipment. All this is done using the Power System Analysis Toolbox (PSAT) to simulate the grid. Afterwards, it is reduced to its equivalent $230 \mathrm{kV} / 500 \mathrm{kV}$ system and simulated in SimPowerSystem (Simulink Library), as well as the control system of the SVC, to obtain the expected behavior of the SNI with Var Compensators. Observing the improvement of the system, higher stability, and reduction in voltage jeopardize. To end up migrating the simulation from SimPowerSystem into the ARTEMIS Library to get the opportunity to implement it in the future on the Opal-RT Real-Time simulator.

articleTitle: Research on Loop-closing in Distribution Networks Based on a New Single-core Asymmetric Phase-shifting Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Power supply reliability of distribution networks can be improved by loop-closing operations, but there is a risk of feeder overcurrent tripping. Existing loop-closing devices are characterized by complex structure, large size, high cost, and low compensation accuracy. Therefore, a loop-closing device based on a New Single-core Asymmetric Phase Shifting Transformer (NSAPST) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the topology and input-output voltage characteristics of the NSAPST are introduced. Secondly, a typical loop-closing network model for distribution networks based on NSAPST is established. Finally, the loop-closing transfer of distribution networks based on NSAPST is verified through PSCAD/EMTDC numerical simulation and actual case analysis. The simulation results indicate that the loop-closing transfer method of distribution networks based on NSAPST is safer and more reliable compared to direct loop-closing.

articleTitle: Research on Transformer Hot Point Tracing Based on Distributed Optical Fiber Temperature Measurement Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper presents a method of optical fiber placement for a 10 kV transformer. The process closely attaches the optical fiber to the outer surface of the winding and uses the spiral layout from bottom to top, subsequently, the fiber-optic insulating paper and the white cloth strip are used for secondary fixing. This arrangement is aimed at effectively preventing the optical fiber position deviation caused by the normal vibration of the transformer without changing the insulation structure of the transformer. Through the temperature rise test of the 10 kV transformer and the monitoring of each phase temperature by using ROTDR technology, the test results show that the temperature of three-phase winding increases with the increase of winding height, however, the temperature of the top winding decreases because of better heat dissipation conditions. It is found that the local hot spots of high voltage windings occur at $77.78 \%$, $77.78 \%$, and $88.89 \%$ of the windings height of $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{B}$, and C respectively in the rated current application stage of the temperature rise test, the hot spot temperatures were $83.18{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, $80.32^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $81.6^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ respectively. Among them, the a-phase hot spot temperature is the highest, possibly because the hot spot is located in a, B two-phase gap, the oil flow impact caused the temperature rise.

articleTitle: Research on Improved Dual-Modulation Wave Neutral-Point Voltage Balancing Control Strategy of Three-Level STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) has the advantages of fast reactive current regulation, bidirectional continuous reactive power adjustment, and low harmonic content, making it highly promising for application. The Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) topology, due to its low cost, reduced losses, easy control, and good output waveform, is widely used. However, this structure suffers from DC-side bus neutral-point voltage imbalance. This paper first analyzes the causes of NPC neutral point voltage imbalance, which are attributed to voltage fluctuations caused by the charging and discharging process during the $\mathbf{O}$ state. Subsequently, an improved dual modulation wave neutral point balancing control strategy is proposed. This strategy initially injects zero-sequence voltage to enhance the utilization of DC voltage. Then, by employing a dual modulation wave method based on zero-level decomposition, it adjusts the duty cycle of the zero level to eliminate the neutral point voltage imbalance. Furthermore, to reduce switching losses, the angle intervals for zero-level decomposition are provided for both inductive and capacitive reactive power outputs of STATCOM. Finally, simulations are conducted to validate the correctness and effectiveness of this strategy.

articleTitle: Advancing Electric Vehicle Load Estimation for Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) challenges electric distribution grids due to increased demand and the need for efficient grid management. This paper introduces a methodology to estimate future EV charging loads considering electric, socioeconomic, transport, and household factors. By combining Monte Carlo simulations with regression models, we analyze EVs’ spatial distribution and charging demand in Santiago, Chile. Our main methodological contribution is the integration of Monte Carlo simulations, multivariate linear regression, and spatial analysis to provide nuanced estimations of EV charging demand in different substations. This approach accounts for variability and enhances the reliability and usability of our estimations. Incorporating stochastic variables allows the examination of different EV penetration and usage scenarios, offering insights into their distribution network impacts. This method improves demand estimation, which is key for grid management and infrastructure planning. Our flexible methodology can be applied to various urban and energy contexts, facilitating the adaptation of electrical infrastructure for electric mobility.

articleTitle: Utilizing IOTA Distributed Ledger Platform for Security in Model Predictive Frequency Control System of Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for renewable energy sources has increased significantly, and microgrids have emerged as an effective solution for integrating renewable energy sources into the power grid. In microgrid systems, distributed control is crucial for ensuring reliable and efficient operation. However, conventional control systems have limitations such as a single point of failure, security vulnerabilities, and lack of trust between different stakeholders. A common type of attack is the false data injection attack (FDIA). The proposed system utilizes smart contracts and the Tangle, a data structure used by the Internet of Things Application (IOTA), to enable secure and efficient data exchange among different stakeholders in the microgrid. The system also employs the IOTA token, which allows for secure and transparent transactions among different parties. Ultimately, case studies are introduced to confirm that the proposed hierarchical blockchain system is a robust solution for securing the control system and enhancing the advantages for prosumers. The numerical results illustrate the effectiveness and practicality of the approach.

articleTitle: Empirical Analysis of Financial Transmission Right Trading Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Financial transmission rights (FTRs) serve as important financial instruments for risk mitigation and congestion arbitrage in the electricity market. Although substantial research has investigated the bidding strategies associated with many market products such as energy, ancillary services and virtual bids, a comprehensive study from a proprietary trading company (PTC)’s perspective for FTRs is lacking. To fill the research gap, this paper investigates the bidding strategies of PTCs in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO)’s annual FTR auctions from 2021 to 2022. First, we develop a matching algorithm to map asset owner identification numbers to entity codes of PTCs. Then, we deploy the K-medoids clustering algorithm to analyze the FTR bidding behavior of the top 10 PTCs. Our study identifies a unique approach used by some PTCs that leverages an unconventional strategy to arbitrage the differences between settlement prices of FTRs between rounds of the annual auction.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Grid-Tied Photovoltaic Inverter with Net Metering Using IoT for Enhanced Power Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The global transition away from fossil fuels is gaining momentum to prevent environmental degradation, and as the supply gap for electricity deepens, so does the quest for alternative power generation technologies. Solar energy utilizing PV cells is one potential approach in this endeavor. This technology, which uses renewable resources, represents a massive step towards sustainability. In light of issues like insufficient energy production and unstable power distribution, there is an urgent need to control and regulate electricity use properly. As the demand for sustainable power in homes and businesses is growing, existing utility systems strive to meet it, prompting a search for more intelligent methods to consume energy. This study proposes a grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) inverter with net metering as an effective way to integrate solar energy generation with existing power infrastructures. The analysis for the proposed scheme is carried out using Proteus software, which provides information about the system’s functionality and how it might help alleviate power shortages and reduce the stress on utility networks. Additionally, this technology encourages a more sustainable approach to electricity usage by enabling distributed generation (DG), which improves energy self-sufficiency. The results demonstrate that grid-tied PV net metering that utilizes IOT significantly reduces energy shortages and ensures a longerlasting, environmentally responsible infrastructure. Finally, the proposed study plays a critical role in realizing a future powered by renewable resources.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Resilience of Urban Energy Systems in Multi-Energy Micro-grid Via Preventive and Corrective Intelligent Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With the increase of occurrence frequency and severity of power outages, the urban micro-grid is gradually established to resist the impact of emergency events. The multienergy micro-grid (MEMG) can further enhance resilience of urban energy systems, however, the cooperative operation of multi-energy sectors to enhance the resilience needs further optimization in the MEMG. In this paper, the normal operating mode of the multi-energy micro-grid and island operation mode under disaster conditions have been modeled, aiming to minimize costs through the coordinated optimization of operating equipment such as distributed generation (DG), combined heat and power (CHP), storage and so on. Furthermore, we have designed an intelligent overall operational strategy that includes preventive and corrective controls. This strategy optimizes the dispatch of local resources, reducing the curtailment of essential loads during disasters, thereby enhancing the resilience of urban energy systems.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy System Optimization and Pricing Analysis on V2G
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With increasing energy demand and sustainability goals, there would be additional pressure on the domestic energy supply capability to meet such demands, and poor energy supply would potentially lead to power shortages, blackouts, and even irreversible consequences. To deal with such an issue, we proposed an optimization model for maximizing the power output of a hybrid energy system, meanwhile, the adoption of renewable energies is guaranteed in the formulation as well as minimized costs to prevent the overuse of non-renewable energies. The results indicated that solar power possesses the greatest potential in generating clean power, accounting for $29.1 \%$ of the total power output. In addition, a pricing analysis on vehicle-to-gird is built to visualize the relationship between the reselling price and the reselling amount, so that it serves as a secondary power source to further compensate for the increasing energy demand. By conducting such an analysis, both V2G agents can benefit either by recognizing the required budget to purchase extra power or by understanding the potential profit of reselling energy via V2G. This work sheds light on improving the amount of power generated, future energy policies on transitioning to renewable energies, pricing implications, and potential market framework for realizing the true potential of vehicle-to-grid technologies.

articleTitle: Joint Convolutional Neural Network and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit Model for False Data Injection Attacks Detection in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: False data injection attack (FDIA), as a kind of covert cyber attack, can be secretly tampered with measurement data to steal power or destabilize the operation of the smart grid. With the upgrading of monitoring equipment, the amount of data in the smart grid is getting bigger, and the feature vectors are getting more and more complex. To further improve the detection performance of FDIA, this paper combines convolutional neural network (CNN) with bidirectional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU) to construct a new hybrid detection model. The model integrates the features of CNN and Bi-GRU can better extract data features, i.e., CNN adopts a layer-by-layer structure to extract data features, and Bi-GRU acts as a bi-directional network to capture both past and future information, and ultimately outputs the hidden state at each time step. We take a small smart grid as an example to simulate and verify the FDIA detection effect of different models, where the dataset comes from the phasor measurement units. The results show that for varying levels of attack intensity, CNN-Bi-GRU model consistently maintains high detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Clean Energy-farming Model under Uncertainty Using Stochastic Optimization and Life Cycle Cost Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimization model for clean energy planning in farming that takes uncertain future projections into account. A stochastic optimization model is applied to determine optimal energy and farming equipment combinations, considering scenarios of uncertainty under multiple farming area sizes. The energy mixes comprise solar photovoltaic panels and battery storage to provide electricity to farm-related equipment, which is categorized into two types by their load usage pattern, including daily-load and periodic-load. A mixed-integer scenario-based stochastic optimization model is developed to minimize the life cycle costs of the optimal solutions through the expected economic life. A case study of a remote cacao-growing site in northern Thailand is presented. The empirical results proved the economies of scale, demonstrating that the larger the farm, the more energy-efficient it becomes; however, the correlation is not linear. The life cycle cost analysis findings from the objective function indicated that, given the listed uncertainties, the average levelized cost of electricity could be reduced to 0.217 USD/kWh. The proposed model could contribute to an emissions reduction in the agricultural sector of up to $1,417.86 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{CO}_{2}$-eq annually per hectare of farmland. The empirical findings in this study offer quantitative support for decision-makers seeking off-grid clean-energy planning for remote horticulture sites while efficiently accounting for uncertainty.

articleTitle: POE20-Biobutanol Blends Fueled for a CRDI Diesel Engine as a Renewable Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Diesel mixed 20% palm oil esters (POE20) is being developed as an alternative fuel to replace regular diesel. POE20 cannot use for common rail direct injection (CRDI) diesel engines, since its viscosity are higher than regular diesel. Reducing viscosity of POE20 by adding alcohols and adjusting fuel injection pressure (FIP) of CRDI diesel engines are continuously studied. Biobutanol is better physical properties than some alcohols. Thus, the main aim of the research is to study the physical properties of POE20 mixed with biobutanol increased until $20 \%$. Next, there are the experimental studies of a CRDI diesel engine at a constant speed and a FIP lower than 600 bar under various loads, when operated with the POE20-biobutanol blends compared with POE20 and regular diesel. This work found that the POE20 mixed with $20 \%$ biobutanol was lower density and viscosity than POE20, and similar to regular diesel. Outstandingly, it was better performance and emission characteristics than regular diesel and POE20. Electrical power and brake thermal efficiency were increased up to $1.3 \%$ and $7.4 \%$, respectively. The releases of carbon monoxide, black smoke, and nitric oxide were decreased up to $\mathbf{2 2. 6 1 \%}, \mathbf{1 5. 8 5 \%}$, and $\mathbf{1 4. 4 1 \%}$, respectively.

articleTitle: Modeling and Small-signal Stability of Microgrid with Virtual Synchronous Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Microgrids with high penetration levels of InverterBased Resources (IBRs) are gaining popularity due to their flexibility and potential for integration with renewable energy sources. However, the presence of IBRs significantly alters system dynamics, leading to new control and stability challenges. The Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) model is a promising approach to standardize the behavior of IBRs, enhancing microgrid controllability and stability. To implement this model efficiently, it is essential to analyze the stability of both the VSG and the microgrid, particularly focusing on small-signal stability. This paper develops a small-signal model of an IBR equipped with a VSG controller and a comprehensive model of the entire microgrid. The methodology includes mathematical modeling and simulation to evaluate stability across various operating conditions. The stability analysis provides insights into the system’s dynamic behavior and offers specific recommendations for designing the VSG controller to optimize system stability. Key findings indicate that precise tuning of the VSG parameters can effectively improve microgrid performance.

articleTitle: Topological reconfiguration in Distribution Systems for loss minimization considering load-ability constraints through a group search algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The amount of electrical energy losses in distribution systems depends on the amount of current that flows through the conductors and their caliber; they affect the quality of energy; therefore, in this investigation, a possible solution to this problem is proposed. In the present work, a heuristic methodology is proposed for the minimization of losses in the feeders of a distribution network using a heuristic method for topological reconfiguration with the opening and closing of link switches already established in each distribution network using an algorithm. For group search, since this is a complex combinatorial problem, it is proposed to use a reconfiguration algorithm that will analyze all the possible configurations that will be subjected to power flows to obtain the state of the system. An efficient reconfiguration in distribution networks depends on the methodology to be implemented. It must comply with the restrictions such as maintaining radiality and supplying the entire load. This document provides information regarding the group search algorithm and the flow load based on backward/forward sweep in three distribution systems of 33 bars, 69 bars, and 136 bars.

articleTitle: Japanese Household Electric Power Consumption and Power Supply Mode Optimization Model Based On Neural Network and Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This study employs neural networks and linear programming to optimize household electricity consumption and auxiliary power supply modes in Japan, aiming to enhance energy efficiency and reduce carbon dioxide emissions. Using TensorFlow, the neural network predicts electricity consumption based on local meteorological data, and these predictions are optimized via linear programming. The dataset covers six years, with five years allocated for training and one year for testing. The results demonstrate that the neural network accurately predicts household electricity consumption, maintaining daily fluctuations within 20 watts. Power supply optimization can lower monthly energy costs by 30%, improving distribution efficiency, fostering green energy development, and reducing household energy expenses.

articleTitle: Voltage Quality Improvement for Hybrid Energy Storage of DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: DC microgrids (MGs) have recently garnered significant interest due to their efficient power conversion and simpler control systems compared to AC MGs. However, managing DC MGs presents specific challenges, especially when dealing with pulsed power loads and constant power loads, as both require rapid dynamic responses from the MG, impacting voltage quality. This paper introduces a novel control methods, including a highpass filter with model predictive control (MPC) for current distribution between the battery and supercapacitor (SC) and a neuro-fuzzy system, to address these issues. These methods adjust the SC’s state of charge (SoC) following abrupt load changes and maintain its SoC within a predefined range to ensure continuous operation.
