Using the proposed feedback neuro-fuzzy technique, the MG can improve voltage quality and transient response, achieving results that are nearly identical to those of the MPC. Simulations conducted in MATLAB/Simulink confirm the effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Interval Estimation-Based Detection of the False Data Injection Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Nowadays, cyber system composed of sensing and communication devices plays a vital role in modern power system, which makes cyber attack a great threat. False data injection attack (FDIA) is a typical kind of cyber attack, which has been widely studied because it can bypass the bad data detection mechanism. This paper proposes an interval estimation-based detection method for FDIA. The load prediction results based on autoregressive moving average model and state prediction results based on Kalman filter are used in the interval estimation model to calculate the upper and lower limits of the branch power measurements. Consequently, the FDIA can be detected if any of the measurements exceed the upper or lower limits. In addition, a bilevel programming model for FDIA in microgrids with droop controlled distributed generation is established. Simulation results validate the accuracy of the proposed method for FDIA detection.

articleTitle: Grid Forming-based Hydrogen System for High-penetration Renewable Energy Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Significant changes are anticipated in how energy is produced and utilized in the future. Many experts see microgrids as pivotal players in this shift. Microgrids offer enhanced reliability and resilience, along with cleaner energy. They are designed to operate in conjunction with distributed energy resources such as solar panels, fuel cells, and battery storage. These DERs are often more dependable and environmentally friendly compared to traditional energy sources. Among available energy storage systems, hydrogen emerges as a suitable solution due to its high power density and potential for bidirectional energy flow. It helps to enhance the electrical grid by employing gas-to-power solutions through fuel cells and storing excess electrical energy via power-to-gas electrolyzers. This paper introduces an islanded microgrid model comprising a controllable fuel cell system connected to an AC load through power electronic devices. The system undergoes operation under varying load conditions to assess the performance of fuel cells as grid-forming units and the microgrid’s stability under the designed control structure. The results demonstrate that the proposed fuelcell system can operate autonomously without reliance on the main grid, in various conditions, from no-load to short-term overload. Moreover, they also verified the system performance of the proposed system under unbalanced load scenario. Overall, the results proved that the designed PEMFC distributed generator can remain stable under various working condition and temporary electrical faults.

articleTitle: High-Performance Voltage Control for Dual-ThreePhase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators: Ensuring Stability Over a Wide Speed Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative voltage regulation control strategy for a wide-speed-range double threephase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) under dynamic load conditions. The strategy is based on the variance of the voltage squared as an input to the outer loop ProportionalIntegral (PI) controller. A method for determining the voltage loop control parameters that adapt to variations in motor parameters, controller parameters, and rotational speed is also provided. The study demonstrates that the power generation system maintains excellent voltage tracking and robustness against load disturbances across a broad speed range from 300 to 3800 revolutions per minute (rpm). The implementation of this control strategy has achieved high-performance voltage regulation, effectively addressing a significant challenge in the field. The experimental outcomes validate the accuracy and efficacy of the proposed control strategy, substantiating its practical applicability and potential for industrial implementation.

articleTitle: Charging Cost Minimization in a Fleet Depot Using Adaptive Queuing
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of scheduling electric vehicle ($\mathbf{E V}$) charging in fleet depots, considering diverse vehicle schedules and service commitments. The rising adoption of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) has driven interest in fleet electrification, offering a path for fleet owners to achieve greenhouse gas reduction targets. A key component of this transition is a reliable smart charging solution for fleet depots. We formulate the EV fleet charging cost minimization problem, considering tiered service routes for vehicles and a limited number of on-site chargers. An innovative approach using an Adaptive Queue (AQ)-based Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithm is proposed for online scheduling. This method prioritizes critical vehicles to ensure service continuity. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the AQ-MPC algorithm reduces charging costs while delivering $10-15 \%$ more energy to priority vehicles compared to a standard MPC approach. Furthermore, it maintains system stability within constrained charging networks, whereas uncontrolled charging leads to significant instability.

articleTitle: Determining Hosting Capacity of Low-Voltage Distribution System with High Penetration of Electric Vehicles by Monte Carlo-Based Quasi-Dynamic Simulation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The integration of electric vehicles (EVs) with renewable energy and energy storage systems (ESSs) becomes fundamental for sustainable electricity grids and transportation. This research introduces a sophisticated charging management approach aimed at assessing the hosting capacity of EVs within multi-energy systems incorporating solar photovoltaic (PV) generation and ESSs. This methodology integrates quasi-dynamic and Monte Carlo simulations, facilitating comprehensive evaluations of various scenarios and uncertainty behavior of EV users. Additionally, this paper proposes the implementation of smart charging algorithms designed to mitigate overload issues concerning a distribution transformer and feeders, along with corrective measures for undervoltage violations at customer load points. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EV charging methodology, a 14-bus low-voltage distribution system with solar PV rooftops and ESSs is utilized as a case study. The simulations were carried out using DIgSILENT PowerFactory, comparing the outcomes between uncoordinated and smart charging scenarios. The results indicate that the proposed charging strategy enhances the system’s EV hosting capacity while simultaneously satisfying the operational constraints.

articleTitle: Research on Energy Consumption Management of Electric Vehicles Based on Different Methods and Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With the construction of ecological civilization and the proposal of the dual-carbon goal, the public’s awareness of environmental protection continues to improve, and the production and sales of electric vehicles in China continue to grow explosively, ranking first in the world for eight consecutive years. Therefore, the energy consumption of the electric vehicle has gradually become a hot social concern. This paper compares three conversion methods and results for energy consumption of electric vehicles, analyzes the energy consumption status of electric vehicles in China, including battery electric vehicles and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, and evaluates the impact of different conversion methods on the corporate average fuel economy, providing methods and data basis for energy consumption management of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Sand-Based Thermal Energy Storage for Thermal Solar Systems in the UAE
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to investigate the feasibility of using sand as a storage media for low-to-high temperature Thermal Energy Storage (TES) technologies. The study involved collecting sand samples from various locations in the UAE (desert, mountain, and beach), to measure and analyze their thermophysical properties. The results showed that the specific heat capacity, thermal conductivity, and dry density of sand are significantly influenced by factors such as particle size distribution, initial water content, and geographical location, which affects the elemental content. Desert sand appeared as a better option for TES, due to its relatively higher specific heat, thermal conductivity, and dry density. Copper was added to the sand in different forms and percentages to improve its thermal conductivity. The property tests indicated a promising increase in thermal conductivity, along with a decrease in specific heat capacity.

articleTitle: Double-layer Optimal Dispatching of Low-voltage Zone Based on Carbon Flow Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Under the background of the current carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goal, in order to promote the transformation of power system to low-carbon, this paper puts forward a low-carbon dispatching strategy based on carbon flow model, focusing on the low-voltage zone of power system. Firstly, the nodes of the complex network are simplified by using the principle of carbon flow, and a carbon emission flow model is constructed to perceive the changing law of carbon potential of major nodes in each time period. Secondly, the calculation model of carbon emission flow is integrated into the dispatching mechanism of the zone, and the equipment dispatching scheme and the energy consumption guidance scheme of the zone are formulated, based on which a double-layer optimal dispatching model of the low-voltage zone based on the carbon flow model is formed. The upper model focuses on the low-carbon dispatching of the zone, while the lower model involves the economic dispatching of users. Finally, the effectiveness of the optimized scheduling strategy in the low voltage zone is verified by field tests.
